input: Submit my short film to a festival

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether the film is fully finished or still in post-production determines whether the plan starts with completion tasks or goes straight to submission prep.
Whether this is a solo project or involves a team/collaborators affects who needs to provide materials like release forms, bios, or sign off on submissions.
The genre, theme, or subject of the film determines which festivals are the best fit — genre-specific, regional, or broad-audience festivals.
Submission fees vary widely per festival; knowing the budget for fees determines how many festivals to target and which platforms to use.
Some filmmakers prioritize prestige (e.g., Sundance, SXSW), others want high acceptance odds, local exposure, or specific audience types — this shapes the festival shortlist entirely.
Whether the goal is a single submission or a multi-festival run changes the scale of the plan and how submission deadlines are tracked.
Most festivals use platforms like FilmFreeway or Withoutabox; knowing if the user has an account and a ready screener link determines the immediate first action.

gold.taskTitle: Submit short film to a festival
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to submit their completed (or in-progress) short film to a film festival, which involves selecting the right festival, preparing materials, and completing the submission process.

questions.title: Is your short film fully finished and ready to screen?
questions.description: Determine whether the film is picture-locked, color-graded, and has final audio — or if post-production work still needs to happen before submission.

questions.title: What genre or subject is your short film?
questions.description: Identify the film's genre, theme, or subject matter so the plan can target festivals that are the best programmatic fit.

questions.title: What is your total budget for submission fees?
questions.description: Establish how much money is available to spend on entry fees, which typically range from free to $100+ per festival, to determine how many submissions are realistic.

questions.title: Do you have a specific type of festival in mind?
questions.description: Understand whether the user is aiming for prestigious tier-one festivals, genre-specific events, regional/local festivals, or simply wants the widest exposure possible.

questions.title: Are you submitting to one festival or building a full run?
questions.description: Clarify whether this is a single targeted submission or a multi-festival campaign, which determines the complexity of deadline tracking and materials management.

questions.title: Do you already have a FilmFreeway or submission platform account?
questions.description: Find out if the user is set up on the main submission platforms and has a screener link ready, to identify the true immediate next action.

questions.title: Did anyone else work on the film who must approve the submission?
questions.description: Determine if collaborators, co-directors, producers, or rights holders need to provide materials or sign off before the film can be officially submitted.
